text:
Maria: quick sync — we need a decision on how to expose burst/queue behavior in the API and console. Customers keep getting 429 in some cases and 503 in others; it's confusing.
Sam: agree. Current behavior: per-key quota breaches => 429, global router overload => 503. But users expect consistent guidance.
AJ: we should consider a two-tier strategy: early local reject (429) when per-key tokens are empty, and a soft-queue (with ETA) when the request is within a global capacity window but we can buffer. That avoids hammering backed services.
Kelly: telemetry matters here — if we add soft-queue we must add metrics: per-key.shed_count, per-org.queue_entered, queue_wait_p50/p95/p99, and route_level.shed_rate. Console needs a panel that ties shed events to rolling deploys.
Ryan: rollout UX idea: feature flag the soft-queue by org, start with 10% traffic or a canary org list. Also expose a header so SDKs can surface queue state to apps.
Maria: headers proposal: X-RW-Queue-Pos, X-RW-Queue-ETA, Retry-After for 429/503. For soft-queue we'll return 202 with a body explaining ETA and a request_id to poll. Thoughts on 202 vs 200+stream?
Sam: prefer 202 for queued (non-blocking) and a small polling endpoint /queue/status. Streaming keeps connections open and hurts gateway concurrency. 202 + ETA is simpler for clients.
AJ: fairness note — bursts should be leveled across keys in an org. Idea: per-key token buckets + an org-level smoothing window. If key depletes but org pool has credits, allow borrow until org cap. If org cap depleted -> queue or reject. Pseudocode:
```
# per-request on arrival
if key.tokens >= cost:
  serve()
elif org.tokens >= cost and borrow_allowed(key):
  borrow_and_serve()
elif global.available_capacity > threshold:
  enqueue(request)
else:
  return 503
```
This avoids punishing a heavy key if org has spare capacity.
Kelly: how do we instrument borrow events? We need a metric for borrow_count and borrow_latency to detect noisy neighbors. Also a graph for per-org effective concurrency vs shard capacity.
Maria: agree. Also need clear API error body so support can explain: sample:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "code": "rate_limited",
  "message": "Per-key burst exhausted",
  "retry_after": 3,
  "help": "Consider retrying with exponential backoff or request a higher quota",
  "request_id": "r_abc123"
}
```
And for queued:
```
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
{
  "code": "queued",
  "message": "Request queued due to transient load",
  "queue_eta": 120,
  "queue_position": 42,
  "request_id": "q_456def"
}
```
Ryan: for SDKs we should add a small helper that intercepts 202 and does exponential poll with backoff and a max wait config. Document it in the console and show per-org queue hit rate.
ops: deploy-bot: routing-service v2.3.1 deployed @ 1819901500 :rocket:
Maria: thanks — after v2.3.1 we can toggle soft-queue behind a flag and run a 10% canary on staging orgs.
Sam: one more open question: for private deployments, do we keep same headers and endpoints? I'd prefer consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private so client behavior is uniform.
AJ: agreed — only difference is operator-controlled thresholds. Private installs can cap borrowing. We'll add config knobs: org_borrow_enabled, max_borrow_fraction, queue_enabled.
Kelly: I'll mock up console tiles: 1) "Queue health" (depth, p95 wait, processed/sec), 2) "Shed events" (429/503 by route), 3) "Borrow usage" (per-org heatmap). Will post tomorrow.
Ryan: schedule a rollout plan doc? I'll create a short RFC: /docs/rfcs/queue-and-shed-guidelines (canary plan, metrics, SDK changes).
Maria: action items: AJ implement borrow + queue proof-of-concept, Kelly console mocks, Sam telemetry metric names and alerts, Ryan RFC and SDK helper, Ops to prepare canary list.
Sam: alert ideas: high borrow_ratio > 0.2 for 1m, queue_p99 > 30s, sudden spike in per-key 429s.
AJ: one last thought — for some idempotent endpoints we can accept longer queue time; for non-idempotent we should bias to 429. We'll add endpoint-level hints (idempotency metadata).
Maria: perfect. Let's reconvene Friday after Kelly posts mocks and AJ demo. :thumbsup:
__notes: Follow agents.md: no title field included, messages in single continuous string, metadata fields present.
